status: Design only. No production Lua or native bridge has been added.

observed_current_boundary.finding: The spike exposes an in-process C pointer ABI only. It does not open a socket/FIFO, serialize commands, retain a Lua job identity, or implement a release deadline.

lib/rhythm_doctor/state_machine.lua.cancel_then_release: lines 87-96: invalidate token, on_cancel(old token), then nonblocking on_release(owner token)
lib/rhythm_doctor/state_machine.lua.release_ack: lines 74-81: resources_released validates owner token before pending project work continues

lib/project_lifecycle.lua.project_transition: lines 23-30 waits on capture_guard:prepare_project_change and shows RELEASING CAPTURE when deferred
lib/project_lifecycle.lua.gap: There is no controller bridge or timeout; a release acknowledgement is currently injected by tests/host code.

existing_lua_anchors.mosaic.lua: No state-machine construction or native capture bridge is wired in this checkout; integration must first add a dedicated owner rather than placing blocking I/O in grid/key callbacks.
existing_lua_anchors.planned_terminal_transitions: Root is adding state_machine:capture_failed(token,error) and state_machine:capture_timeout(token,valid_span). The controller must call them only for an exact active full identity; it does not edit the machine.

proposed_controller.construction: capture_controller.new({ transport_stopped, now_monotonic, schedule_once, unschedule, native_client, machine, report_status })
proposed_controller.responsibility: The controller alone performs nonblocking bridge I/O and owns one native-capture job. State-machine callbacks only call controller methods; the JACK callback and Lua event thread never wait for each other.
proposed_controller.job_identity: Mint opaque job_id on every preflight/start. Every request and reply carries {protocol_version, job_id, project_id, generation, analysis_revision}. Reject a reply unless all five fields equal the controller active job and the state-machine token. A superseded token can never release or publish a newer job.
callback_wiring: on_capture_start(mode, token): require an already successful preflight for token; send START with the full identity. If it is rejected, report NOT READY and call capture_failed only for that exact token.

on_analyse(token): for an ordinary Finish, send STOP then poll until COMPLETED and PUBLISH. Start the analysis worker only after a matching PUBLISHED reply validates frame count, rate, start/end frames and identity. For a timeout-valid capture, reuse its already-published asset; never stop or publish a different job.
terminal native failure: on a matching FAILED state/error, call machine:capture_failed(token,error). That method owns FAILED/release behavior; the controller must not manufacture resources_released.

automatic 45-second completion: publish the completed capture, obtain valid_span only from the separate acquisition result for the same identity, then call machine:capture_timeout(token,valid_span). An invalid span retains the published audio for alignment; a valid span lets the machine enter ANALYSING and invoke on_analyse.
on_cancel(old_token): send CANCEL once for that exact identity; ignore all later completion/publish replies for it.

on_release(owner_token): send RELEASE once. On a matching RELEASED reply, call machine:resources_released(owner_token, transport_stopped()) exactly once. Never acknowledge release from a bare socket close or mismatched identity.

bridge_protocol.transport: A private local Unix-domain sequenced-message socket owned by a small native helper that owns rd_capture pointers. Lua sends length-bounded JSON or line-delimited JSON; no FIFO because cancellation/reply association and backpressure need framed bidirectional messages.
bridge_protocol.rule: The helper maps job_id to its rd_capture pointer and destroys it only after C-level cancellation/deactivation has completed. It must refuse a duplicate job_id and an operation whose identity differs from the mapped job.

bounded_release_timeout.start: When on_release dispatches RELEASE, schedule one monotonic 2-second deadline tied to that exact full identity.
bounded_release_timeout.success: Only a matching RELEASED reply cancels the deadline and calls resources_released.
bounded_release_timeout.timeout: Show CAPTURE RELEASE TIMEOUT, retain the pending project transition and resource lease, and offer retry/diagnostic. Do not call resources_released and do not load/save a project while ownership is unproven. This bounds Lua waiting without falsely claiming a live JACK callback or worker is gone.
bounded_release_timeout.late_reply: A matching later RELEASED reply may complete release; a stale/mismatched reply is recorded and ignored.

required_red_green_coverage_before_wirin: State-machine/controller test: stale START, COMPLETED, PUBLISHED and RELEASED replies cannot mutate a replacement project or generation.
Release deadline test: project continuation remains deferred at 2 seconds and no resources_released call occurs; matching later release completes once.
Cancel-vs-stop and transport-start tests: cancellation invalidates identity before bridge I/O; a late completion cannot launch analysis.
Protocol test with an independent fake helper: bounded frame size, malformed reply rejection, duplicate job rejection, and exactly-once release acknowledgement.
Native integration test: helper command sequence exercises the existing C API without altering pre-existing JACK graph state.

terminal_event_ordering.timeout_valid: C capacity COMPLETED -> PUBLISH -> matching acquisition valid_span=true -> capture_timeout(token,true) -> on_analyse(token) using the same asset.
terminal_event_ordering.timeout_invalid: C capacity COMPLETED -> PUBLISH -> matching acquisition valid_span=false -> capture_timeout(token,false); retained asset is available to Alignment and normal release proceeds only through on_release.
terminal_event_ordering.failed: C FAILED/error -> controller identity check -> capture_failed(token,error) -> machine on_release -> RELEASED -> resources_released.
